body:
Pass 15. Left residual-statistics.R alone - it was 11 seconds old. Verified the padding foundation instead.

Good news: your target property already holds. Fixed width 32, blocks of 8 vs 16 -> bitwise identical, max|diff| = 0, and the padded tail residualizes to exactly zero.

One hazard at the padded/unpadded boundary: residual_block() and .residual_padded_block() do not always agree, because residualizing the padded matrix is a different GEMM shape. features=4 at widths 16/32/64 differs by 4.44e-16; features=8 and 13 agree bitwise at every width. Same kernel-selection effect, different boundary.

So: use read_padded exclusively inside metric construction (mixing readers turns plan-independence into reader-dependence), and if you write a test that the two readers agree, give it a tolerance - identical() would pass at 8 and 13 and fail at 4, looking flaky. Details on the bead.
